cloud-data-exfiltration
objects.description: A leaked SSH private key leads to theft of ML training data from an AWS account. A developer pushes a private key to a GitHub repository, and secret scanning raises an alert under three minutes later. Five minutes after the push a new IP logs into an EC2 development host with the key, steals the instance role's credentials from the IMDSv2 metadata service, enumerates IAM roles and S3, syncs a training-data bucket (65 objects) to the host, and pulls about 507 MB back over SFTP (526 MB of flow-log egress). The developer later resolves the alert and pushes a follow-up commit. Neither step revokes the key or the role credentials. Five telemetry sources must be correlated: GitHub organization audit, the host's auth.log, CrowdStrike Falcon Data Replicator events from the host, AWS CloudTrail, and VPC flow logs. 348,963 events over 71 hours (2026-10-11 01:00 to 2026-10-14 00:00 UTC), mostly account and internet background, with the intrusion on 2026-10-13 between 18:50 and 19:47 UTC.

objects.name: S1 Leaked private key found in a public repository
objects.description: A developer pushes an SSH private key to the datalake-utils repository at 18:50:14 UTC. GitHub secret scanning raises an ssh_private_key alert at 18:52:41. Evidence: github_audit git.push and secret_scanning_alert.create.

objects.name: S2 SSH login to the dev host with the leaked key (T1021.004)
objects.description: At 18:55:44 a new IP (54.193.215.120) logs in as the developer with the leaked key (publickey authentication), using the account as a valid account. Evidence: linux_auth Accepted publickey, VPC flows to port 22. The account's legitimate sessions, including one ending at 18:52 the same day, all come from 75.125.237.59.

objects.name: S2 SSH login to the dev host with the leaked key (T1078)
objects.description: Part of stage S2: SSH login to the dev host with the leaked key.

objects.name: S3 Host discovery (T1082)
objects.description: At 18:56:42 the intruder runs id, hostname, uname -a, reads os-release and lists the home directory. Evidence: crowdstrike_fdr ProcessRollup2.

objects.name: S3 Host discovery (T1033)
objects.description: Part of stage S3: Host discovery.

objects.name: S4 Instance role credentials stolen from IMDSv2
objects.description: At 18:58:12 curl requests an IMDSv2 token and then the instance role credentials from 169.254.169.254. Evidence: crowdstrike_fdr command lines.

objects.name: S5 Cloud identity, IAM and S3 discovery with the stolen role
objects.description: From 18:59:23 an aws cli unpacked under /var/tmp runs sts get-caller-identity, s3 ls, iam get-role, list-attached-role-policies and list-roles, and is denied ec2 describe-instances. The calls come from the instance public IP 13.57.16.209. Evidence: aws_cloudtrail under the model-dev-05-readonly role, plus matching crowdstrike_fdr commands.

objects.name: S6 Training-data bucket listed and synced to the host
objects.description: At 19:02:43 the intruder lists jn-model-training-data-5233, and at 19:04:43 to 19:04:45 runs aws s3 sync into ~/data. That is 65 GetObject calls and about 514 MB of S3 ingress. Evidence: aws_cloudtrail ListObjects and GetObject, aws_vpc_flow from S3 prefixes, crowdstrike_fdr.

objects.name: S7 Data exfiltrated over SFTP
objects.description: At 19:07:42 a second key login opens an SFTP session that reads 7 files (about 507 MB per sftp-server) at 19:07:43 to 19:07:46. VPC flow shows 526,475,698 bytes out to 54.193.215.120. Evidence: linux_auth sftp-server, aws_vpc_flow.

objects.name: S8 Alert resolved without revoking access
objects.description: At 19:22:46 the developer resolves the secret-scanning alert, then pushes at 19:42:12 and fetches at 19:46:27. Nothing in the data shows the key being removed from authorized_keys or the role credentials being revoked. Evidence: github_audit.
